subject: Dedicated capacity pilot — SLO & hardware concurrency walkthrough
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity pilot — SLO & hardware concurrency walkthrough

Jordan,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. This thread captures the follow-up items we promised on sizing a Dedicated (reserved) pilot to validate latency and throughput SLOs.

Summary of what I heard:
- Target latency: p95 <= 200 ms for short-chat streaming (partial outputs acceptable); p95 <= 350 ms for long-completion requests.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 150 concurrent requests (mostly streaming), with burst requirements up to 500 concurrent short requests for 30–90s.
- Model family: open LLaMA-2 variant (30B) for most cases; a smaller 7B falls back for low-latency paths.
- Average request payload: 1.2k tokens (prompt + context), avg response tokens ~120 for chat; peak response length up to 1k tokens in batch jobs.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability; final acceptance run to use synthetic traffic + a 24-hour soak.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share a representative workload sample (we discussed ndjson export) — we'll use it to generate a validation matrix.
2) We run a three-day pilot in our Dedicated staging cluster comparing: H100 80GB float16, A100 80GB int8/q4oz, and 2xA10Gs for cost/throughput tradeoffs.
3) For each hardware profile we will measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (reqs/s), GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also test streaming tail-latency under burst.
4) We produce a one-page decision doc with recommended reserved throughput (reqs/s), concurrency ceiling, and fallback model routing.

Questions for you to confirm:
- Is the p95 <= 200 ms requirement for short-chat strict (hard SLO) or a stretch goal? 
- Do you have a preferred quantization baseline (we can test int8 + q4 variants) or should we default to preserving 8-bit accuracy for Q3 workloads?
- Any constraints on encryption/KMS usage during the pilot (we can run with customer-managed keys in Private but for Dedicated staging we typically use AWS KMS)?

I'll put Ben on the thread to coordinate the runbook and schedule the test windows.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0142

Attachment: sample-validation-template.csv (stub)
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pilot — SLO & hardware concurrency walkthrough

Karthik,

Appreciate the clear recap — that's aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications and I'm attaching the workload export.

Notes:
- The p95 <= 200 ms is a firm internal target for the "quick-chat" use case (triage messaging); for longer diagnostics workflows we can accept up to 400 ms.
- Bursts are a hard requirement; our busiest windows are 08:30–09:15 and 18:00–18:45 PST, where we see sudden fan-in. We need predictable tail behavior.
- We do not have a strict quantization preference; accuracy is more important than marginal cost savings for diagnostic outputs. If results show accuracy loss, we'll prioritize accuracy.
- KMS: we can provide a customer-managed key via AWS if needed. Pilot data is non-PHI but sensitive; SOC2 + audit logs are required.

Attached: acme_workload_sample.ndjson (4.2 MB) — includes synthetic anonymized traces.

Best,

Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Health
j.ellis@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme_workload_sample.ndjson (stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pilot — SLO & hardware concurrency walkthrough

Jordan,

Thanks for the workload sample — importing now. Quick note on the validation matrix I mentioned:
- We'll construct experiments across three axes: hardware (H100 / A100 / A10G), model precision (fp16 / int8 / q4), and routing policy (single-model vs two-tier fallback to 7B).
- For reserved throughput we'll propose an initial commit of 500 reqs/s (steady-state 150 concurrency) with a burst capacity buffer of +250 reqs/s configured at autoscale thresholds.
- Operationally, we'll run the following checks:
  * Streaming tail-latency under burst (10s windows),
  * KV cache hit-rate impact for repeated contexts,
  * Backpressure behavior when GPUs saturate (queue vs reject policy),
  * Cost per 1M tokens estimate for each hardware.

I'll attach the draft validation matrix and a quick-run instructions doc. If that plan is OK, we will schedule a kickoff next Monday at 09:00 PST for a 60-minute sync and reserve a two-day test window the following week.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood
ben@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_validation_matrix.csv (stub)
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pilot — SLO & hardware concurrency walkthrough

Ben,

Plan looks great — Monday 09:00 PST works and we'll lock a two-day window (Aug 17–18) for the pilot. I will loop in procurement (cc'ing Alicia Park) to discuss reserved throughput commitments and timing — we anticipate a Q3 procurement decision.

Two quick asks prior to kickoff:
1) Can you confirm whether the pilot runs will use customer-managed KMS? If not, we'll need to sign an exception form.
2) Please include a short checklist of the metrics you'll surface in the post-pilot decision doc (p95/p99, GPU util, cost per 1M tokens, streaming tail-latency percentiles, and concurrency saturation points).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Jordan

Cc: Alicia Park <apark@acmehealth.com>
